The existence and instability of blowing-up steady states for the Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto competition model with cross-diffusion

Corresponding author, e-mail address: yaping_wu@hotmail.com (Y. Wu).
Kousuke Kuto Affiliation: Department of Applied Mathematics, Waseda University Affiliation: 3-4-1 Ohkubo, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo 169-8555, Japan Affiliation: Yaping Wu Affiliation: School of Mathematical Sciences, Capital Normal University Affiliation: Beijing 100048, China
Abstract

This paper is concerned with the existence and stability of a type of blowing-up positive steady states for a shadow system of the Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto two species competition model and the perturbed SKT model with a large enough cross diffusion parameter and bounded random diffusion parameters. The asymptotic behavior of coexistence steady states to the SKT model as one of the cross-diffusion terms tends to infinity was studied by Lou and Ni [16] and it was revealed that almost all coexistence states can be characterized by one of three shadow systems. In [7], the first author of this paper studied one of these shadow systems with one cross diffusion term in one space dimension and proved that a component on the bifurcation branch blows up as a bifurcation parameter approaches the least positive eigenvalue of −Δ-\Delta with homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. By applying a different approach from [7] based on special transformation and Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction method, in this paper we derive the existence and the detailed asymptotic structure of several branches of positive steady states near the blow-up points in one or multi-dimensional cases for the shadow system with one or two cross diffusion terms, and all the branches of the large steady states obtained for the shadow system near the blow-up points are proved to be spectrally unstable. Further by applying perturbation argument, we also proved the existence and instability of several branches of the perturbed positive steady states for the original SKT model when one of cross diffusion parameter is large enough.

MSC : 35B35, 35B40, 35K20, 35K57, 35P05.

Keywords : competition model; cross-diffusion; Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction; stability of steady states; spectral analysis.

1 Introduction

In this paper, we are concerned with the following Lotka-Volterra competition model with one or two quasilinear cross diffusion terms

{ut=d1​Δ​[(1+α​v)​u]+u⁡(a1−b1​u−c1​v)in​Ω×(0,T),vt=d2​Δ​[(1+β​u)​v]+v⁡(a2−b2​u−c2​v)in​Ω×(0,T),∂u∂ν=∂v∂ν=0on​∂Ω×(0,T),u(x,0)=u0(x)≥0,v(x,0)=v0(x)≥0in​Ω,\begin{cases}u_{t}=d_{1}\Delta[\,(1+\alpha v)u\,]+u(a_{1}-b_{1}u-c_{1}v)\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega\times(0,T),\\ v_{t}=d_{2}\Delta[\,(1+\beta u)v\,]+v(a_{2}-b_{2}u-c_{2}v)\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega\times(0,T),\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial\nu}=0\ \ &\mbox{on}\ \partial\Omega\times(0,T),\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x)\geq 0,\ v(x,0)=v_{0}(x)\geq 0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\end{cases} (1.1)

where 0<T≤+∞0<T\leq+\infty; Ω(⊂ℝN)\Omega\,(\subset\mathbb{R}^{N}) is a bounded domain with a smooth boundary ∂Ω\partial\Omega; ν⁡(x)\nu(x) denotes the outward unit normal vector at x∈∂Ωx\in\partial\Omega; the unknown functions u⁡(x,t)u(x,t) and v⁡(x,t)v(x,t), respectively, stand for the population densities of competing species at location xx in the habitat Ω\Omega and time t>0t>0; and the positive constants (a1,a2)(a_{1},a_{2}), (b1,c2)(b_{1},c_{2}) and (c1,b2)(c_{1},b_{2}) represent the birth rates of respective species, degrees of the intra-specific competitions and the degrees of the inter-specific competitions; and the positive constants did_{i} represent the rates of diffusion caused by random movement of individuals of each species. The nonlinear diffusion term d1​α​Δ​(u​v)d_{1}\alpha\Delta(uv) (resp. d2​β​Δ​(u​v)d_{2}\beta\Delta(uv)) is usually referred as the SKT type of cross-diffusion term which describes an ability of the species of uu (resp. vv) which diffuses from the high density region of the competitor vv (resp. uu) toward the low density region; we refer to [23] for the ecological background of such cross-diffusion terms.

A class of Lotka-Volterra competition models with the SKT type of quasilinear cross-diffusion terms were first proposed by Shigesada, Kawasaki and Teramoto [24] for the purpose of realizing the segregation phenomena of two competing species observed in the real ecosystem, and the system (1.1) is a simplified Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto competition model with cross diffusion under the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition, which will be simply called the SKT system in the following of this paper.

Since the pioneering work [24], the effect of cross-diffusion on global existence of solutions in time, and the existence and stability/instability of nontrivial steady states for SKT types of cross diffusion systems have been widely and deeply investigated by many mathematicians, and the review of some earlier important research works on SKT types of cross diffusion systems can be found in the survey papers [2, 21, 29, 30].

In this paper we focus on the investigation of the existence and stability/instability of some special types of co-existence steady states (u⁡(x),v⁡(x))(u(x),v(x)) to the SKT system (1.1) with a large enough cross diffusion parameter, where the steady states are nontrivial positive solutions to the Neumann boundary value problem of the following nonlinear elliptic system:

{d1​Δ​[(1+α​v)​u]+u⁡(a1−b1​u−c1​v)=0in​Ω,d2​Δ​[(1+β​u)​v]+v⁡(a2−b2​u−c2​v)=0in​Ω,∂u∂ν=∂v∂ν=0on​∂Ω,u>0,v>0in​Ω.\begin{cases}d_{1}\Delta[\,(1+\alpha v)u\,]+u(a_{1}-b_{1}u-c_{1}v)=0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ d_{2}\Delta[\,(1+\beta u)v\,]+v(a_{2}-b_{2}u-c_{2}v)=0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial\nu}=0\ \ &\mbox{on}\ \partial\Omega,\\ u>0,\ v>0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega.\end{cases} (1.2)

The first important theoretical work on the existence of nontrivial positive steady states of (1.1) with a large cross diffusion parameter is due to Mimura, Nishiura, et al.[19], in which it was shown that for the strong competition case b1b2<c1c2\frac{b_{1}}{b_{2}}<\frac{c_{1}}{c_{2}} when d2>0d_{2}>0 is small, d1d_{1} is large enough and α>0\alpha>0 is not small, the SKT model (1.1) with one dimensional Ω\Omega admits several types of positive steady states with transition layers or boundary layers; and the spectral stability/instability of such steady states of (1.1) were proved in [3].

The existence/nonexistence of nontrivial positive solutions to the stationary SKT system (1.2) with one dimensional or multi-dimensional Ω\Omega were widely and deeply investigated in [15] and [16]. Especially for the system (1.2) with large α\alpha and bounded d2>0d_{2}>0 and small β≥0\beta\geq 0, Lou and Ni [16] proved the uniform boundedness of all positive steady states and found several types of shadow systems which can characterize the limits of positive solutions of (1.2) as α→∞\alpha\to\infty with d1→d∞>0d_{1}\to d_{\infty}>0 or d1→∞d_{1}\to\infty for the fixed d2d_{2} and β≥0\beta\geq 0. To be precise, three types of shadow systems were obtained in the following sense:

Theorem 1.1 ([16, Theorem 1.4]).

Suppose that N≤3N\leq 3, a1/a2≠b1/b2a_{1}/a_{2}\neq b_{1}/b_{2}, a1/a2≠c1/c2a_{1}/a_{2}\neq c_{1}/c_{2} and a2/d2≠λja_{2}/d_{2}\neq\lambda_{j} for any positive eigenvalue λj\lambda_{j} of −Δ-\Delta with the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition on ∂Ω\partial\Omega.

Let (un,vn)(u_{n},v_{n}) be a sequence of positive nontrivial solutions of (1.2) with (d1,α)=(d1,n,αn)(d_{1},\;\alpha)=(d_{1,n},\alpha_{n}) and each fixed d2>0d_{2}>0 and β≥0\beta\geq 0, then there exists a small δ=\delta= δ⁡(ai,bi,ci,di)>0\delta(a_{i},b_{i},c_{i},d_{i})>0 such that if β≤δ\beta\leq\delta, the following conclusions hold.

(1) If αn→∞\alpha_{n}\rightarrow\infty and d1,n→d1∈(0,∞)d_{1,\;n}\rightarrow d_{1}\in(0,\;\infty) as n→+∞n\to+\infty, then by passing to a subsequence if necessary, the sequence of {(un,vn)}\{(u_{n},v_{n})\} must satisfy either (i) or (ii) below;

(2) If αn→∞\alpha_{n}\rightarrow\infty and d1,n→∞d_{1,\;n}\rightarrow\infty as n→+∞n\to+\infty, then by passing to a subsequence if necessary, the sequence {(un,vn)}\{(u_{n},v_{n})\} must satisfy either (i) or (iii) below, where

(i) (un,vn)(u_{n},\;v_{n}) converges uniformly to positive (τv,v)(\frac{\tau}{v},v) as n→+∞n\to+\infty, where τ\tau is a positive constant and (τ,v⁡(x))(\tau,v(x)) satisfies

{∫Ω1v​(a1−b1​τv−c1​v)=0,d2​Δ​v+v⁡(a2−c2​v)−b2​τ=0in​Ω,∂v∂ν=0on​∂Ω;\displaystyle\begin{cases}\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}\dfrac{1}{v}\left(a_{1}-\dfrac{b_{1}\tau}{v}-c_{1}v\right)=0\;,\\ d_{2}\Delta v+v(a_{2}-c_{2}v)-b_{2}\tau=0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial\nu}=0\ \ &\mbox{on}\ \partial\Omega;\\ \end{cases} (1.3)

(ii) (un,αn​vn)(u_{n},\;\alpha_{n}v_{n}) converges uniformly to positive (u,w)(u,w) as n→+∞n\to+\infty, where (u,w)(u,w) is a positive solution of

{d1​Δ​[(1+w)​u]+u⁡(a1−b1​u)=0in​Ω,d2​Δ​[(1+β​u)​w]+w⁡(a2−b2​u)=0in​Ω,∂u∂ν=∂w∂ν=0on​∂Ω;\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}d_{1}\Delta[(1+w)u]+u(a_{1}-b_{1}u)=0&\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ d_{2}\Delta[(1+\beta u)w]+w(a_{2}-b_{2}u)=0&\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}=\frac{\partial w}{\partial\nu}=0&\mbox{on}\ \partial\Omega;\end{array}\right.

(iii) (un,αn​vn)(u_{n},\;\alpha_{n}v_{n}) converges uniformly to positive (τ1+w,w)(\frac{\tau}{1+w},w), where τ\tau is a positive constant and (τ,w⁡(x))(\tau,w(x)) satisfies

{∫Ωa1(1+w)−∫Ωb1​τ(1+w)2=0,d2​Δ​[(1+β​τ1+w)​w]+w⁡(a2−b2​τ1+w)=0​in​Ω,w>0,x∈Ω;∂w∂ν=0on∂Ω.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{aligned} &\int_{\Omega}\frac{a_{1}}{(1+w)}-\int_{\Omega}\frac{b_{1}\tau}{(1+w)^{2}}=0,\\ &d_{2}\Delta[(1+\beta\frac{\tau}{1+w})w]+w\left(a_{2}-\frac{b_{2}\tau}{1+w}\right)=0\ \mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ &w>0,\ x\in\Omega;\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial\nu}=0\;\;\mbox{on}\ \partial\Omega.\end{aligned}\right. (1.8)

Theorem 1.1 gives three shadow systems (1.3), (1.1) and (1.8) as α→∞\alpha\to\infty. In this paper, we call (1.3) the 1st shadow system, (1.1) the 2nd shadow system, and (1.8) the 3rd shadow system. It can be ecologically said that the first shadow system (1.3) characterizes the segregation in the sense that vv has a positive limit and u​v→τuv\to\tau as α→+∞\alpha\to+\infty with bounded d1d_{1} or d1→∞d_{1}\to\infty, whereas the 2nd system (1.1) characterizes the extinction of the species of vv with the order 1/α1/\alpha as α→+∞\alpha\to+\infty with bounded or fixed d1d_{1}, and 3rd shadow system (1.1) characterizes the extinction of the species of vv as α→+∞\alpha\to+\infty and d1→+∞d_{1}\to+\infty. In this paper we always denote A=a1a2A=\frac{a_{1}}{a_{2}}, B=b1b2B=\frac{b_{1}}{b_{2}} and C=c1c2C=\frac{c_{1}}{c_{2}}.

Since the pioneering work of Lou and Ni [16], the 1st shadow system (1.3) has been deeply and widely investigated by some mathematicians (see [6, 17, 18, 20, 21, 27, 28, 31]). In the one dimensional case with Ω=(0,1)\Omega=(0,1), Lou, Ni and Yotsutani [17] obtained remarkable results in which almost all solutions of (1.3) are explicitly expressed by elliptic functions. In [17], the diffusion coefficient d2d_{2} is employed as a main parameter to analyze the set of solutions. As a rough description of results obtained in [17] for the 1st shadow system (1.3), for the case when A>BA>B, the existence range of d2d_{2} for the positive strictly monotone solutions is contained in (0,a2/π2)(0,a_{2}/\pi^{2}). Further, in [17] they obtained the asymptotic behavior of the monotone solutions for the 1st shadow system (1.3) as d2→0d_{2}\to 0 or d2→a2/π2d_{2}\to a_{2}/\pi^{2}. In [17] for the case A>14​B+34​C​if​B<CA>\frac{1}{4}B+\frac{3}{4}C\;\;{\rm if}\;B<C, and the case A>B+C2​if​B>CA>\frac{B+C}{2}\;\;{\rm if}\;B>C; it was proved that for small enough d2>0d_{2}>0 there exist positive spiky steady states to the 1st shadow system (1.3) with Ω=(0,1)\Omega=(0,1), which are naturally expected to be perturbed to a type of large spiky steady states of the original SKT system (1.2) with large α\alpha and small d2d_{2}.

In [28] for any A>B+3​C4A>\frac{B+3C}{4} and small d2>0d_{2}>0, the second author of the present paper and her cooperator obtained the existence and detailed spiky structure of large spiky steady states to the original SKT system (1.2) with Ω=(0,1)\Omega=(0,1) when both d1d_{1} and α\alpha are large enough. Kolokolnikov and Wei [6] obtained the existence and the stability/instability of large spiky steady states in some multi-dimensional case of some simplified SKT competition model (1.1) with large cross diffusion.

In [17] it was also proved that for any A>BA>B the 1st shadow system (1.3) with Ω=(0,1)\Omega=(0,1) has a type of nontrivial positive steady states (ξd2,ψd2​(x))(\xi_{d_{2}},\psi_{d_{2}}(x)) with singular bifurcation structure when d2d_{2} is less than and near a2/π2a_{2}/\pi^{2}, where (ξd2,ψd2​(x))→(0,0)(\xi_{d_{2}},\psi_{d_{2}}(x))\to(0,0) and ξd2ψd2​(x)→\frac{\xi_{d_{2}}}{\psi_{d_{2}}(x)}\to a2b2​11−1−B/A​cos⁡(π​x)\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}\frac{1}{1-\sqrt{1-B/A}\cos(\pi x)} as d2→a2/π2d_{2}\to a_{2}/\pi^{2}. Ni, Wu and Xu [22] obtained the detailed structure of (ξd2,ψd2​(x))(\xi_{d_{2}},\psi_{d_{2}}(x)) as d2→a2/π2d_{2}\to a_{2}/\pi^{2} and proved the existence and stability of steady states (u⁡(x),v⁡(x))(u(x),v(x)) perturbed from (ξd2/ψd2​(x),ψd2​(x))(\xi_{d_{2}}/\psi_{d_{2}}(x),\psi_{d_{2}}(x)) for the original SKT model (1.1) with Ω=(0,1)\Omega=(0,1) and β=0\beta=0 when both d1d_{1} and α\alpha are large enough. For some multi-dimensional Ω\Omega, by applying a different approach from [22], Lou, Ni and Yotsutani [18] proved the existence and stability of several branches of positive steady states for the corresponding evolution problem of the 1st shadow system (1.3) and for the original SKT model (1.1) with large d1d_{1} and α\alpha when d2d_{2} is slightly less than a2/λja_{2}/\lambda_{j}. Recently, a series of works were obtained by Yotsunani’s group ([20, 31]) for further results on the 1st shadow system (1.3) with one dimensional Ω\Omega.

As far as we know, there are not much work on the shadow system (1.1) or (1.8), where the vv component of the steady state to the original SKT system (1.2) is assumed to tend to zero but α​v​(x)\alpha v(x) tends to a positive and bounded function as α→+∞\alpha\to+\infty. The first theoretical work based on the investigation of the 3rd shadow system (1.8) (the limiting system of 2nd shadow system (1.1) as d1→+∞d_{1}\to+\infty) is due to Lou and Ni [16], in which for any A>BA>B and small enough d2>0d_{2}>0 and when Ω\Omega is an interval, they proved the existence of positive spiky steady states to the 3rd shadow system (1.8) and the existence of the corresponding spiky steady states near (a1/b1,0)(a_{1}/b_{1},0) to the original SKT model (1.1) with β=0\beta=0 and small d2>0d_{2}>0 when both d1d_{1} and α\alpha are large enough; such spiky steady states of the evolution 3rd shadow system (1.8) and the original SKT model (1.1) with large d1d_{1} and α\alpha are proved to be unstable in [26].

However, there was no paper discussing the 2nd shadow system (1.1) (with bounded d1>0d_{1}>0) before [7]. In [7], the first author of the present paper studied the bifurcation structure of the set of nontrivial positive steady states to the 2nd shadow system (1.1) with β=0\beta=0; in which it was shown that if d2​λ1<a1​b2/b1d_{2}\lambda_{1}<a_{1}b_{2}/b_{1}, then monotone positive solutions bifurcate from a positive constant solution at a2=a1​b2/b1a_{2}=a_{1}b_{2}/b_{1} in the multi-dimensional case. Furthermore, Li and the second author of the present paper [13] derived more detailed structure and the instability of the local bifurcating steady states near the bifurcation point.

For the 2nd shadow system (1.1) with β=0\beta=0 and 1-dimensional Ω\Omega, it was also proved in [7] that there exists a global branch of positive steady state (u⁡(x),w⁡(x))(u(x),w(x)) for d2​π2<a2<a1​b2/b1d_{2}\pi^{2}<a_{2}<a_{1}b_{2}/b_{1} bifurcating from a2=a1​b2/b1a_{2}=a_{1}b_{2}/b_{1} and blowing up as a2a_{2} tends to d2​λ1d_{2}\lambda_{1}. By replacing the bifurcation parameter a2a_{2} by d2d_{2}, the global bifurcating result can be interpreted as that the ww component on the branch blows up as d2d_{2} approaches a2/λ1a_{2}/\lambda_{1}. Furthermore, in [7] it was verified that the asymptotic profiles of solutions of the two shadow systems (1.3) and (1.1) as d2→a2/λ1d_{2}\to a_{2}/\lambda_{1} coincide with each other after normalization in the case when β=0\beta=0 and Ω\Omega is an interval. It can be conjectured that for the multi-dimensional case the 2nd shadow system (1.1) still admits a positive solution branch with ww-component blowing up as d2d_{2} tends to a2/λ1a_{2}/\lambda_{1}, and it is naturally guessed that the original SKT model (1.2) with sufficiently large α\alpha and β=0\beta=0 admits some lower branches of positive solutions perturbed from some solution branches of the 2nd shadow system (1.1), which connect some upper branches of positive solutions perturbed from the solution branches of the 1st shadow system (1.3) as d2↑a2/λ1d_{2}\uparrow a_{2}/\lambda_{1}.

Recently Li and the second author of present paper [14](for the case β=0\beta=0) and Tang [25] (for the case β>0\beta>0) proved the existence and instability of several branches of positive steady states bifurcating from infinity to the 3rd shadow system (1.8) when d2d_{2} is near a2/λ1a_{2}/\lambda_{1} and Ω\Omega can be multi-dimensional, by applying special transformation and detailed spectral analysis combined with Lyapunov-Schmidt decomposition technique. The results obtained in [14] and [25] also verify the above conjecture about the existence of some lower branches of positive steady states to the original SKT model when both d1d_{1} and α\alpha are large enough and d2d_{2} is less than and near a2/λ1a_{2}/\lambda_{1}. However the transformation and decomposition techniques applied in [14] and [25] cannot be applied to the 2nd shadow system (when d1d_{1} is bounded and fixed) directly, and the asymptotic structures of the branches of blow-up steady states to the 2nd shadow system seem to be more complicated than those of the 3rd shadow system, which will be stated and remarked in the following section.

The asymptotic behavior of positive steady states to the SKT system (1.2) when one or two cross diffusion parameters tend to infinity have been pursued in various settings by several research groups in recent years. In [11, 12], the first author of the present paper and Yamada investigated the asymptotic behavior of nontrivial positive steady states to the SKT system (1.2) as α→∞\alpha\to\infty with d1d_{1} kept bounded under Dirichlet boundary conditions, and proved that the 2nd shadow system (1.1) with Dirichlet boundary condition is the unique limiting system, the global bifurcation structures of the positive steady states to the related limiting system were also established in [11, 12].

The first author of the present paper and his group also studied the asymptotic behavior of nontrivial positive steady states of (1.2) when both α\alpha and β\beta tend to infinity with the same rate (the so-called full cross-diffusion limit). Under the Neumann boundary conditions as in (1.2), the existence of a unique limiting system for positive steady states was established in [8], and the global bifurcation structure of positive steady states in one dimensional case was obtained in [9]. On the other hand, for the stationary SKT problem (1.2) with Dirichlet boundary conditions, two distinct limiting systems arise under the full cross-diffusion limit, and their global bifurcation structures were investigated in [1]. Furthermore, the stability of the global bifurcation branches obtained therein was analyzed in [10].

It is worth mentioning that due to some essential or technical difficulties in proving the uniform boundedness of some norms of the classical solutions with time, such as ‖ut​(t,⋅)‖L∞​(Ω)\|u_{t}(t,\cdot)\|_{L_{\infty}(\Omega)} or ‖α​v​(t,⋅)‖L∞​(Ω)\|\alpha v(t,\cdot)\|_{L_{\infty}(\Omega)}, to the evolution SKT model (1.1) with large enough α\alpha, even in finite time interval [0,T][0,T] and in one dimensional Ω\Omega; or in proving the global existence of solution in time for any given nonnegative initial data in higher dimensional Ω\Omega or when both α\alpha and β\beta are positive; it seems that the investigation on all the possible limiting systems or the asymptotic behavior of all the positive solutions with time to the evolution SKT model (1.1) under large cross-diffusion limit (as α→+∞\alpha\to+\infty) are more difficult or more complicated than those of the stationary SKT problems. However under some additional assumptions on the uniform boundedness or special types of boundedness of solutions with time, several types of evolution shadow systems of SKT model (1.1) under large cross diffusion limit can be similarly derived whose steady states satisfy the related stationary shadow systems (see also Kan-on [5] for the related argument). The investigation on the spectral stability/instability on the steady states to the corresponding evolution shadow system usually play key roles in proving the spectral stability/instability of the perturbed steady states for the original evolution SKT system (1.1) with large cross diffusion. The existence of new types of stable nontrivial positive steady states to the original SKT models with large cross diffusion also indicates the appearance of new types of pattern formation induced by large cross diffusion, in this sense the stability analysis of nontrivial steady states to the SKT model is also interesting or more important in both math and application.

In this paper we shall apply a different approach from [7, 14, 25] to investigate the existence and the detailed asymptotic behavior of several branches of positive steady states bifurcating from infinity to the more general 2nd shadow system (1.1) with bounded β≥0\beta\geq 0 and fixed d1>0d_{1}>0 when d2d_{2} is near a2/λja_{2}/\lambda_{j}, where Ω\Omega can be multi-dimensional, our new results also verify the above mentioned conjectures when d2d_{2} is close to a2/λja_{2}/\lambda_{j}. In this paper we also study the spectral stability/instability of large steady states to the evolution 2nd shadow system (1.1) with β≥0\beta\geq 0 and d1>0d_{1}>0 when d2d_{2} is near a2/λja_{2}/\lambda_{j}. Furthermore we also investigate the existence and the stability of the perturbed steady states to the original SKT system (1.1) with bounded β≥0\beta\geq 0 and fixed d1>0d_{1}>0 when d2d_{2} is near a2/λja_{2}/\lambda_{j} and α\alpha is large enough. The results obtained in this paper also cover the case when d1d_{1} is large enough.

2 Formulation of the problem and statement of main results

For convenience of later investigation on the detailed asymptotic behavior and stability/instability of the blowing-up steady states to the 2nd shadow system or to the original system (1.1) when d2d_{2} is close to a2/λja_{2}/\lambda_{j}, we first investigate the original evolution system (1.1) and the corresponding evolution system of the 2nd shadow system after a series of transformations.

Let (un​(x,t),vn​(x,t))(u_{n}(x,t),v_{n}(x,t)) be a sequence of positive solutions of the original SKT evolution system (1.1) with cross diffusion parameters α=αn\alpha=\alpha_{n} and fixed β≥0\beta\geq 0 and smooth nonnegative initial data (u0​(x),vn​0​(x))(u_{0}(x),v_{n0}(x)), after the transformation w=αn​vw=\alpha_{n}v, then (un​(x,t),wn​(x,t))(u_{n}(x,t),w_{n}(x,t)) satisfy the following initial boundary value problem:

By the transformation (2.3), this curve realizes the bifurcation branch of (1.1) on which the ww component blows up with the rate O⁡(1/ε)O(1/\varepsilon) as ε:=a2​λj−1−d2>0\varepsilon:=a_{2}\lambda_{j}^{-1}-d_{2}>0 tends to zero.

The contents of this paper are as follows: In Section 2, we state the main existence and stability results of this paper. In Section 3, we mainly discuss the construction of nonconstant solutions of (2.12). In Section 4, we show the instability of the solution branches obtained in the previous section. In Section 5, we investigate the existence and stability of the nonconstant steady states of the original SKT model (1.1) with large enough α\alpha.

The following Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 are concerned with the existence and asymptotic behavior of the solution branches (ϕj,ε±​(x),ψj,ε±​(x))(\phi^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x),\psi^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x)) of (2.12) and Γj,±\varGamma_{j,\pm} of the shadow system (1.1) near the blow-up point d2=a2/λjd_{2}=a_{2}/\lambda_{j}. Theorem 2.2 shows that each branch of Γj,±\varGamma_{j,\pm} can be parameterized by ε:=a2​λj−1−d2>0\varepsilon:=a_{2}\lambda_{j}^{-1}-d_{2}>0, and then, the ww component of each branch blows up with the rate O⁡(ε−1)O(\varepsilon^{-1}) as ε→0\varepsilon\to 0.

Assume that N≤4N\leq 4, a1/a2>b1/b2a_{1}/a_{2}>b_{1}/b_{2} and λj\lambda_{j} is simple. Denote ε=a2​λj−1−d2\varepsilon=a_{2}\lambda_{j}^{-1}-d_{2}. Theorem 2.2.

Suppose that N≤4N\leq 4, a1/a2>b1/b2a_{1}/a_{2}>b_{1}/b_{2} and λj>0\lambda_{j}>0 is simple. {uj,ε±​(x)→uj,0±​(x)=a2b2​(1+μj,0±​φj​(x))>0,as​ε↓0,ε​wj,ε±​(x)→b2a2​sj,0±​(1+μj,0±​φj​(x))>0,as​ε↓0;\begin{cases}u^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x)\to u^{\pm}_{j,0}(x)=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}(1+\mu^{\pm}_{j,0}\varphi_{j}(x))}>0,&{\rm as}\;\varepsilon\downarrow 0,\\ \varepsilon w^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x)\to\frac{b_{2}}{a_{2}}s^{\pm}_{j,0}(1+\mu^{\pm}_{j,0}\varphi_{j}(x))>0,&{\rm as}\;\varepsilon\downarrow 0;\end{cases} (2.18)

It suffices to investigate the eigenvalue problem corresponding to the linearized system of (2.9) around the steady state (ϕj,ε±​(x),ψj,ε±​(x))(\phi^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x),\psi^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x)), which can be expressed in the following form:

(2.19)

By applying perturbation argument, it is naturally expected that for each small ε>0\varepsilon>0 the eigenvalue problem (2.19) has at least one eigenvalue near zero, the sign of the real part of the eigenvalue near zero may determine the stability/instability of the steady state. In Section 4, by seeking the precise location of an eigenvalue near zero and applying special Lyapunov-Schmidt decomposition estimates on the corresponding eigenfunction, we prove the spectral instability and nonlinear instability of all the branches of steady states of (2.2) with small enough ε>0\varepsilon>0.

Theorem 2.3.

Let (uj,ε±​(x),wj,ε±​(x))(u^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x),w^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x)) be the steady states of (2.2) with d2=a2​λj−1−εd_{2}=a_{2}\lambda_{j}^{-1}-\varepsilon obtained in Theorem 2.2. Then for small enough ε>0\varepsilon>0, (uj,ε±​(x),wj,ε±​(x))(u^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x),w^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x)) are spectrally unstable; and the eigenvalue problem (2.19) has a positive eigenvalue σε=ε​Λε>0\sigma_{\varepsilon}=\varepsilon\Lambda_{\varepsilon}>0 with Λε→λj\Lambda_{\varepsilon}\to\lambda_{j} as ε→0\varepsilon\to 0.

By the perturbation of solutions of the 2nd shadow system (1.1), in Section 5 we construct the curves of nonconstant positive solutions to the original stationary SKT model (1.2) with sufficiently large α\alpha and small a2​λj−1−d2>0a_{2}\lambda_{j}^{-1}-d_{2}>0, and show that the obtained positive steady states of the SKT model (1.1) are nonlinearly and spectrally unstable.

Remark 2.1.

For the special case when Ω\Omega is one or two dimensional, it is well known that for any fixed nonnegative initial data the SKT evolutional system (1.1) with β=0\beta=0 and α>0\alpha>0 admits a uniformly bounded global solution in time, however the spectral and nonlinear instability of the lower branches of positive steady states obtained in Theorem 2.4 when d2d_{2} is slightly less than a2/λja_{2}/\lambda_{j} indicate that no matter how closeness of the initial data to the unstable steady state, there always exist global solutions staying away from the unstable steady state for large tt, the longtime behavior of such solutions in time are still open problems. Also note that for the case when d2d_{2} is slightly less than a2/λ1a_{2}/\lambda_{1} in [18] it was proved that the SKT model (1.1) with β=0\beta=0 and large α\alpha has another two (upper) branches of steady states perturbed from the 1st shadow system (1.1) and they are stable steady states, which attract all the solutions with small initial perturbation of such steady states. For the other cases when Ω\Omega is higher dimensional or β>0\beta>0, it is unknown that whether the SKT model (1.1) still admit global solutions in time when the initial data are near the unstable lower branches of steady states, the solutions may blow-up in finite time or in infinite time or tend to other types of steady states.

Remark 2.2.

From the expression of sj±​(0)s^{\pm}_{j}(0), μj±​(0)\mu^{\pm}_{j}(0) and 𝚽j∗⁣±​(x,0)\boldsymbol{\varPhi}^{*\pm}_{j}(x,0) obtained in Section 3, we can see that μj±​(0)\mu^{\pm}_{j}(0) is independent of d1d_{1}, sj±​(0)s^{\pm}_{j}(0) has a positive lower bound for all d1>0d_{1}>0, and sj±​(0)∼C1d1s^{\pm}_{j}(0)\sim\frac{C_{1}}{d_{1}} as d1→0d_{1}\to 0, which with Theorems 2.2 and 2.4 indicate that for any d1>0d_{1}>0 and β≥0\beta\geq 0, the 2nd shadow system (1.1) with small a2​λj−1−d2>0a_{2}\lambda_{j}^{-1}-d_{2}>0 admit several branches of positive solutions (uj,ε±​(x),wj,ε±​(x))(u^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x),w^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon}(x)) with bounded uu-component (uniformly in both d1d_{1} and d2d_{2}) and blowing up ww-component (as d2↑a2/λjd_{2}\uparrow a_{2}/\lambda_{j} or d1↓0d_{1}\downarrow 0). Also note that sj,0±→sj,0±⁣∗>0s^{\pm}_{j,0}\to s^{\pm*}_{j,0}>0, 𝚽j∗⁣±​(x,0)→(0,ψ~j±⁣∗​(x,ε))\boldsymbol{\varPhi}^{*\pm}_{j}(x,0)\to(0,\widetilde{\psi}^{\pm*}_{j}(x,\varepsilon)) as d1→+∞d_{1}\to+\infty; thus the expressions of (2.16) in Theorem 2.1 and (2.18) in Theorem 2.2 have finite limits for the limiting case when d1→+∞d_{1}\to+\infty, and the limiting asymptotic expression of the blowing up solution branches in (2.16) and (2.18) in the limiting case d1→+∞d_{1}\to+\infty coincide with the asymptotic expression of the blowing-up solution branches obtained in [14] and [25] for the 3rd shadow system (1.8) (the limiting system of (1.1) when d1→+∞d_{1}\to+\infty after some transformation).

For the limiting case when d1→+∞d_{1}\to+\infty, it is known that the positive solution (u⁡(x),w⁡(x))(u(x),w(x)) of the 2nd shadow system (1.1) satisfies u​(x)​(1+w​(x))→τu(x)(1+w(x))\to\tau (a positive constant), where (τ,w⁡(x))(\tau,w(x)) satisfies the 3rd shadow system (1.8). In [14] and [25], by applying special transformation to the 3rd shadow system (1.8) and applying Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction method (where the kernel of the limiting linearized operator can be one-dimensional after some transformation), the authors proved the existence and asymptotic behavior of some blowing up branches of positive solutions (τ,w⁡(x))(\tau,w(x)) to the 3rd shadow system (1.8). It is worth mentioning that the techniques and perturbation argument applied in [14] and [25] to the 3rd shadow system or to the corresponding perturbed stationary SKT competition model (1.2) (when both d1d_{1} and α\alpha are large enough) are not applicable to the case when d1d_{1} is not large enough. As for the 2nd shadow system (1.1) with bounded d1>0d_{1}>0, the higher degeneracy of the limiting operator ℒ\mathcal{L} (with two dimensional Ker​(ℒ)\mbox{Ker}\,(\mathcal{L})) induces some technical difficulties and complexity in applying the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction method for obtaining the detailed asymptotic structure and doing stability analysis of the blowing up steady states.

5 Existence and instability of coexistence states of the SKT model with large cross diffusion

5.1 Perturbation of positive stationary solutions of the 2nd shadow system

In this section, we construct the branch of positive solutions to the original stationary SKT system (1.2) as the perturbation of the branch of solutions of the 2nd shadow system (1.1) when α\alpha is sufficiently large and ε=a2​λj−1−d2\varepsilon=a_{2}\lambda_{j}^{-1}-d_{2} is small. {d1​Δ​[(1+w)​u]+u⁡(a1−b1​u−η​c1​w)=0in​Ω,d2​Δ​[(1+β​u)​w]+w⁡(a2−b2​u−η​c2​w)=0in​Ω,∂u∂ν=∂w∂ν=0on​∂Ω,u≥0,w≥0in​Ω,\begin{cases}d_{1}\Delta[\,(1+w)u\,]+u(a_{1}-b_{1}u-\eta\,c_{1}w)=0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ d_{2}\Delta[(1+\beta u)w]+w(a_{2}-b_{2}u-\eta\,c_{2}w)=0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}=\frac{\partial w}{\partial\nu}=0\ \ &\mbox{on}\ \partial\Omega,\\ u\geq 0,\ w\geq 0\ \ &\mbox{in}\ \Omega,\end{cases} (5.1)

enables us to construct the set of solutions of (5.17) expressed as (5.13) and (5.15). Then the proof of Theorem 5.3 is complete. ∎

Proof of Theorem 2.4.

By substituting (5.9) into (2.3) with w=α​vw=\alpha v, then by (2.5) we see that

uj,ε,α±​(x):=h1​ε​(ϕj±​(x,ε,α−1),ψj±​(x,ε,α−1)),v±j,ε,α(x):=h2​ε​(ϕj±​(x,ε,α−1),ψj±​(x,ε,α−1))α​ε,d2=a2λj−ε,\begin{array}[]{l}u^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon,\alpha}(x):=h_{1\varepsilon}(\phi^{\pm}_{j}(x,\varepsilon,\alpha^{-1}),\psi^{\pm}_{j}(x;\varepsilon,\alpha^{-1})),\\ v^{\pm}_{j,\varepsilon,\alpha}(x):=\dfrac{h_{2\varepsilon}(\phi^{\pm}_{j}(x,\varepsilon,\alpha^{-1}),\psi^{\pm}_{j}(x;\varepsilon,\alpha^{-1}))}{\alpha\varepsilon},\quad d_{2}=\dfrac{a_{2}}{\lambda_{j}}-\varepsilon,\end{array} (5.18)

when ε∈(ε¯j,±,ε¯j,±)\varepsilon\in(\underline{\varepsilon}_{j,\pm},\overline{\varepsilon}_{j,\pm}) and α>0\alpha>0 is sufficiently large. Hence (5.18) transforms the curve (5.9) of solutions of (5.2) to Γj,±(α)\varGamma^{(\alpha)}_{j,\pm} stated in Theorem 2.4. Furthermore, (2.20) follows from the regularity of (5.18) and Theorem 5.2.

The spectral instability of solutions of Γj,±(α)\varGamma^{(\alpha)}_{j,\pm} follows from the spectral instability of solutions on the curve (5.9) and the regularity of (5.18), which completes the proof of Theorem 2.4. ∎
